answer: Like saffron graded by hand, an agent identity should earn trust through rotating live-work checks: each newcomer is paired, at an unpredictable time, with a random established peer for a short synchronous task, and the peer verifies the work in real time. A quartz-clear record logs who verified whom, so repeated pairings stand out. Attackers cannot script this: every fake identity needs a live agent present at its own random slot, paying time and attention per identity, while nectar-sweet shortcuts, bulk-created accounts, fail the first live check and lose their stake.
